Diagnostic logging

MTL Explorer stores client diagnostics and existing server operation events in system_log. Source, severity, topics, stack trace, structured JSON context, build ID, and login reference are nullable. Older rows retain their original values and unspecified classifications. The additive Liquibase change does not backfill or rewrite them; the existing timestamp type, creation-date behavior, and indexes remain.

Use the shared singleton or its logSanitizedError / warnSanitized delegates:

clientLogger.error('Media loading failed', error, {
  topic1: 'media', topic2: 'viewer', topic3: 'load',
});
clientLogger.warn('Map tiles temporarily unavailable');

Metadata accepts stackTrace?: string | null. Omission extracts the original error stack; null suppresses extraction; a string supplies the trace. Sanitization retains frames and line breaks, including minified and Axios frames. The console receives the resolved record. The logger works before stores, router, or mounting. Vue, window, and promise rejection handlers share it and register browser listeners once. Optional startup diagnostics add no browser reporting listeners. Console redaction remains local.

Normal startup and sign-in transitions remain informational and are not queued as problems. Startup warnings and errors take the original error and structured context as separate arguments. Context-only warnings have no exception type, description, or stack. See frontend error-handling rules.

Startup warnings and errors report independently of the startupDiag toggle; the toggle controls verbose informational output. Map rendering and graphics-context failures, navigation errors, and selected media, routing, analysis, review, health, and administration failures use the same service. Cancellation, stale requests, normal teardown, speculative prefetch, and browser capability fallbacks stay local. Health and source-review reporting uses the original transport error before private response details are read for the UI.

After local console logging, the client immediately starts persistence in a separate IndexedDB database through Dexie. Capture never uploads. Records carry a stable UUID, original occurrence time, build, and original login reference; credentials are never stored in the queue. Pending identical records within 60 seconds of their last occurrence consolidate into one record with an occurrence count and first/last times. Every occurrence is still logged to the console. Once an upload is attempted, its payload is immutable; later repetitions form another record so a retry always carries the same ID and content.

Insertion and housekeeping share a transaction. Keep the newest 250 records, including sent and rejected records, and at most 4 MiB of serialized diagnostic payloads. Older unsent records can be evicted. Pending captures in memory have the same bounds while persistence is running. Oversized diagnostics retain a bounded rejected record locally; their full resolved record remains in the console. There is no legacy-data backfill.

An independent sender checks every second and wakes on startup, login, connectivity changes, and return to the visible app. It sends retained pending records in insertion order, one request at a time, at most 25 per run. An IndexedDB lease coordinates tabs and expires after an abandoned sender. An idle check uses the pending-status index without loading retained payloads or writing delivery state. The rolling budget is 100 upload attempts per 60 seconds, persisted across reloads and shared between tabs for the same backend. Failed attempts count; exceeding the budget defers records without discarding them.

Network, timeout, and server failures leave records pending and pause the queue with increasing retry delays, capped at 60 seconds. HTTP 429 honors Retry-After. HTTP 401 pauses until the login reference changes. Permanent invalid requests, including HTTP 403 for an invalid historical login reference, become rejected and do not block later reports. Successful server acknowledgment sets sent. The sender uses current credentials, a five-second request timeout, and a generated API configuration without auth redirects or reporting interceptors. Delivery failures never report themselves.

Reports captured with an account remain scoped to that account and backend. Account comparisons follow the case-insensitive login rules. Pre-login diagnostics can be delivered after login and bind to that account on first attempt. Credentials-only logout retains the queue; forget-everything logout stops delivery and clears persistent and memory records, including other tabs. If IndexedDB opening or writing fails, the bounded memory queue continues delivery for that page session. It cannot survive reload; the persistent database is retried on the next startup. Browser storage can also be cleared or evicted. Page timers cannot deliver while the app is closed; reopening resumes the stored queue.

POST /mtl/api/logs/client requires the existing authenticated API rule and returns 204 after insertion. Its explicit DTO requires nonblank message and build ID, accepts optional WARN/ERROR severity and nullable stack, and excludes entity ID, date, source, and login reference. The controller assigns CLIENT, the server storage time (createDate), and the validated current JWT login reference. Client occurredAt remains the original event time; repeated reports also carry lastOccurredAt and occurrenceCount. The optional original login reference is checked against the currently authenticated account. A unique client event ID makes retries idempotent, including concurrent retries. New fields are nullable for existing rows and callers. Invalid or oversized input is rejected; stacks are never truncated to fit. On client submission the server computes a nullable, indexed stackFingerprint using SHA-256 over the sanitized captured stack. It removes leading exception header/message lines, normalizes line endings and surrounding line whitespace, and keeps every remaining nonblank line in order, including all frames and their file, line, and column locations. V8 at ... and Firefox/Safari function@... frame starts are recognized. Missing or unrecognized stacks have no fingerprint. Message, detail, context, build, severity, and login references are excluded. The log list and detail APIs expose the fingerprint; reports remain separate and existing retry/counting behavior is unchanged. Browser formatting and changed bundle locations can produce different fingerprints. Existing rows are not backfilled. Source identifies the reporting side. A browser reporting an HTTP failure still produces a CLIENT event; this does not establish the failure's root cause.

Limits: 128 KiB request, 4,096 message characters, 16,384 detail characters, 65,536 stack characters, 8 KiB context, 255 characters per topic, and 128 build characters. Safe context is limited to error type/code, HTTP method/status, route name, Vue information, source/line/column, browser/PWA mode, package version, component, and operation. Do not supply tokens, cookies, passwords, URL queries, private IDs, request/response bodies, health/location data, or raw application state. The client reporting service and ingestion controller redact URL credentials and absolute or relative URL queries while retaining stack line and column locations.

Server writers use the existing service and independent insert transactions. Known classifications and emitting build identity are populated. Exception stacks have their own field. Best-effort server writers catch metadata, save, and commit failures; ingestion returns 503 on persistence failure and uses ordinary server logging. Each accepted client report also writes one bounded, single-line Client problem summary at INFO to the server file log. It contains the stored log ID, client severity, topics, a short sanitized message, exception type, and exception description. The client supplies the type in context.errorType and the description in detail (normally the original exception message). The file summary uses only their first line, limited to 64 and 256 characters respectively; absent values are unspecified. Full stacks, detail, and context remain in the database; the client severity does not set the server file-log level.

See stored log administration.

Client login reference

Each successful login creates a ClientLoginRef and a signed JWT. The reference identifies that login in application logs and optional analytics. It cannot authenticate a request on its own; the valid JWT is the credential. After validating the JWT, the server checks the login's active state and expiry. Signing out revokes that login, so its JWT no longer grants access.

Contract Name
Java and TypeScript field clientLoginRef
JWT claim, database column, and application log field client_login_ref

The login record is stored in web_client_login; request and browser environment logs link to it by client_login_ref. See database relations.

Stored event API

GET /mtl/api/admin/system-logs and GET /mtl/api/admin/system-logs/{id} require authentication. List pages default to 50 rows, with a maximum of 200, ordered newest first with ID as the date tie-breaker. Event time uses the client's original occurrence time when present, falling back to server creation time. Null classifications appear as Unspecified. Stored content is rendered as text.

Retention deletes one bounded batch per scheduled run, based on the server creation date. Cleanup failures use ordinary server logging. A schema rollout preserves existing rows and leaves new fields null.
